verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 11.13
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 11.13

verses.pali: 2. Anussativagga
verses.english: 2. Recollection

verses.pali: Nandiyasutta
verses.english: With Nandiya

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṁ nigrodhārāme.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ vassāvāsaṁ upagantukāmo hoti.
verses.english: Now at that time the Buddha wanted to commence the rains residence at Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Assosi kho nandiyo sakko:
verses.english: Nandiya the Sakyan heard about this,

verses.pali: “bhagavā kira sāvatthiyaṁ vassāvāsaṁ upagantukāmo”ti.
Atha kho nandiyassa sakkassa etadahosi:
verses.english: and thought,

verses.pali: “yannūnāhampi sāvatthiyaṁ vassāvāsaṁ upagaccheyyaṁ.
verses.english: “Why don’t I also commence the rains residence at Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Tattha kammantañceva adhiṭṭhahissāmi, bhagavantañca lacchāmi kālena kālaṁ dassanāyā”ti.
verses.english: There I can focus on my work and from time to time get to see the Buddha.”

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ vassāvāsaṁ upagacchi.
verses.english: So the Buddha commenced the rains residence in Sāvatthī,

verses.pali: Nandiyopi kho sakko sāvatthiyaṁ vassāvāsaṁ upagacchi.
verses.english: and so did Nandiya.

verses.pali: Tattha kammantañceva adhiṭṭhāsi, bhagavantañca labhi kālena kālaṁ dassanāya.
verses.english: There he focused on his work and from time to time got to see the Buddha.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū bhagavato cīvarakammaṁ karonti:
verses.english: At that time several mendicants were making a robe for the Buddha, thinking that

verses.pali: “niṭṭhitacīvaro bhagavā temāsaccayena cārikaṁ pakkamissatī”ti.
verses.english: when his robe was finished and the three months of the rains residence had passed the Buddha would set out wandering.

verses.pali: Assosi kho nandiyo sakko:
verses.english: Nandiya the Sakyan heard about this.

verses.pali: “sambahulā kira bhikkhū bhagavato cīvarakammaṁ karonti:
‘niṭṭhitacīvaro bhagavā temāsaccayena cārikaṁ pakkamissatī’”ti.
Atha kho nandiyo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho nandiyo sakko bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: He went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

verses.pali: “sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante:
verses.english: “Sir, I have heard that

verses.pali: ‘sambahulā kira bhikkhū bhagavato cīvarakammaṁ karonti—
verses.english: several mendicants are making a robe for the Buddha, thinking that

verses.pali: niṭṭhitacīvaro bhagavā temāsaccayena cārikaṁ pakkamissatī’ti.
verses.english: when his robe was finished and the three months of the rains residence had passed the Buddha would set out wandering.

verses.pali: Tesaṁ no, bhante, nānāvihārehi viharataṁ kenassa vihārena vihātabban”ti?
verses.english: Now, we spend our life in various ways. Which of these should we practice?”

verses.pali: “Sādhu sādhu, nandiya.
verses.english: “Good, good Nandiya!

verses.pali: Etaṁ kho, nandiya, tumhākaṁ patirūpaṁ kulaputtānaṁ, yaṁ tumhe tathāgataṁ upasaṅkamitvā puccheyyātha:
verses.english: It’s appropriate that gentlemen such as you come to me and ask:

verses.pali: ‘tesaṁ no, bhante, nānāvihārehi viharataṁ kenassa vihārena vihātabban’ti?
verses.english: ‘We spend our life in various ways. Which of these should we practice?’

verses.pali: Saddho kho, nandiya, ārādhako hoti, no assaddho;
verses.english: The faithful succeed, not the faithless.

verses.pali: sīlavā ārādhako hoti, no dussīlo;
verses.english: The ethical succeed, not the unethical.

verses.pali: āraddhavīriyo ārādhako hoti, no kusīto;
verses.english: The energetic succeed, not the lazy.

verses.pali: upaṭṭhitassati ārādhako hoti, no muṭṭhassati;
verses.english: The mindful succeed, not the unmindful.

verses.pali: samāhito ārādhako hoti, no asamāhito;
verses.english: Those with immersion succeed, not those without immersion.

verses.pali: paññavā ārādhako hoti, no duppañño.
verses.english: The wise succeed, not the witless.

verses.pali: Imesu kho te, nandiya, chasu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya pañcasu dhammesu ajjhattaṁ sati upaṭṭhāpetabbā.
verses.english: When you’re grounded on these six things, go on to establish mindfulness on five further things internally.

verses.pali: Idha tvaṁ, nandiya, tathāgataṁ anussareyyāsi:
verses.english: Firstly, you should recollect the Realized One:

verses.pali: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi, satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
verses.english: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

verses.pali: Iti kho te, nandiya, tathāgataṁ ārabbha ajjhattaṁ sati upaṭṭhāpetabbā.
verses.english: In this way you should establish mindfulness internally based on the Realized One.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ tvaṁ, nandiya, dhammaṁ anussareyyāsi:
verses.english: Furthermore, you should recollect the teaching:

verses.pali: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.
verses.english: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

verses.pali: Iti kho te, nandiya, dhammaṁ ārabbha ajjhattaṁ sati upaṭṭhāpetabbā.
verses.english: In this way you should establish mindfulness internally based on the teaching.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ tvaṁ, nandiya, kalyāṇamitte anussareyyāsi:
verses.english: Furthermore, you should recollect your good friends:

verses.pali: ‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṁ vata me,
verses.english: ‘I’m fortunate, so very fortunate,

verses.pali: yassa me kalyāṇamittā anukampakā atthakāmā ovādakā anusāsakā’ti.
verses.english: to have good friends who advise and instruct me out of kindness and sympathy.’

verses.pali: Iti kho te, nandiya, kalyāṇamitte ārabbha ajjhattaṁ sati upaṭṭhāpetabbā.
verses.english: In this way you should establish mindfulness internally based on good friends.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ tvaṁ, nandiya, attano cāgaṁ anussareyyāsi:
verses.english: Furthermore, you should recollect your own generosity:

verses.pali: ‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṁ vata me,
verses.english: ‘I’m so fortunate, so very fortunate.

verses.pali: yohaṁ maccheramalapariyuṭṭhitāya pajāya vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasāmi muttacāgo payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṁvibhāgarato’ti.
verses.english: Among people with hearts full of the stain of stinginess I live at home rid of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.’

verses.pali: Iti kho te, nandiya, cāgaṁ ārabbha ajjhattaṁ sati upaṭṭhāpetabbā.
verses.english: In this way you should establish mindfulness internally based on generosity.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ tvaṁ, nandiya, devatā anussareyyāsi:
verses.english: Furthermore, you should recollect the deities:

verses.pali: ‘yā devatā atikkammeva kabaḷīkārāhārabhakkhānaṁ devatānaṁ sahabyataṁ aññataraṁ manomayaṁ kāyaṁ upapannā, tā karaṇīyaṁ attano na samanupassanti katassa vā paticayaṁ’.
verses.english: ‘There are deities who, surpassing the company of deities that consume edible food, are reborn in a certain host of mind-made deities. They don’t see in themselves anything more to do, or anything that needs improvement.’

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, nandiya, bhikkhu asamayavimutto karaṇīyaṁ attano na samanupassati katassa vā paticayaṁ;
verses.english: An irreversibly freed mendicant doesn’t see in themselves anything more to do, or anything that needs improvement.

verses.pali: evamevaṁ kho, nandiya, yā tā devatā atikkammeva kabaḷīkārāhārabhakkhānaṁ devatānaṁ sahabyataṁ aññataraṁ manomayaṁ kāyaṁ upapannā, tā karaṇīyaṁ attano na samanupassanti katassa vā paticayaṁ.
verses.english: In the same way, Nandiya, there are deities who, surpassing the company of deities that consume edible food, are reborn in a certain host of mind-made deities. They don’t see in themselves anything more to do, or anything that needs improvement.

verses.pali: Iti kho te, nandiya, devatā ārabbha ajjhattaṁ sati upaṭṭhāpetabbā.
verses.english: In this way you should establish mindfulness internally based on the deities.

verses.pali: Imehi kho, nandiya, ekādasahi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako pajahateva pāpake akusale dhamme, na upādiyati.
verses.english: A noble disciple who possesses these eleven qualities gives up bad, unskillful qualities and doesn’t cling to them.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, nandiya, kumbho nikkujjo vamateva udakaṁ, no vantaṁ paccāvamati;
verses.english: It’s like when a pot full of water is tipped over, so the water drains out and doesn’t go back in.

verses.pali: seyyathāpi vā pana, nandiya, sukkhe tiṇadāye aggi mutto ḍahaññeva gacchati, no daḍḍhaṁ paccudāvattati;
verses.english: Suppose there was an uncontrolled fire. It advances burning up dry woodlands and doesn’t turn back over what it has burned.

verses.pali: evamevaṁ kho, nandiya, imehi ekādasahi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako pajahateva pāpake akusale dhamme, na upādiyatī”ti.
verses.english: In the same way, a noble disciple who possesses these eleven qualities gives up bad, unskillful qualities and doesn’t cling to them.”

verses.pali: Tatiyaṁ.
